phase_task.goal: Budgeted retrieval API — the metered primitives the agent will use to navigate the repo without dumping files into the model. Every retrieval is token-accounted against the ledger, deterministic enough to replay, and passes retrieved code through a secret-redaction boundary. NO agent loop, NO model calls yet (Phase 4).

deliverables.d: Implement RetrievalService (replace the Phase-0 stub) over the Phase-1 index: search_symbols, definition, references, read_span, list_dir, structural_grep. Each returns a metered RetrievalResult (content + token/byte accounting).

Token accounting on EVERY call, charged to the budget_ledger: reading a whole file costs strictly more than reading a span; the cost is a function of bytes/tokens actually returned. Reserve/commit against the ledger so an over-budget retrieval is refused, not served-then-charged. A retrieval that would exceed remaining budget fails cleanly (BudgetExceeded) without returning content.

Determinism for replay: the same query against the same workspace snapshot returns byte-identical results AND identical token/byte accounting. This is what lets Phase 4 replay a run. Assert cross-call determinism in a test.

Secret redaction at the retrieval boundary: retrieved content is scrubbed of secrets (the planted .env/config.py fake secrets, and a defensible secret-pattern set) BEFORE it leaves the retrieval layer — so secrets can never reach a prompt or output downstream. read_span over the file containing a fake secret returns the code with the secret value redacted; the redaction is logged/metered as an event. Test this against the Phase-1 planted secrets.

read_span returns precise line/byte spans (not whole files) with enough surrounding structure to be useful; span requests are the primary primitive and the cheapest path. Returning a whole file must be possible but visibly more expensive.

Wire the primitives into agentctl for operator inspection (e.g. agentctl retrieve search/read/refs), showing the token/byte cost of each call. Internal/operator only — still NOT a consumer HTTP API (that is Phase 6).

phase_task.oracle: On the sample repo, via make test (new unit + integration tests, no model/network): (1) read_span of a 10-line span costs strictly fewer tokens/bytes than reading the whole file — assert the inequality; (2) same query + same snapshot => byte-identical result AND identical accounting across calls; (3) a retrieval whose cost exceeds remaining ledger budget raises BudgetExceeded and returns NO content and charges nothing (ledger unchanged); (4) read_span over the planted-secret file returns redacted content — the fake secret VALUE never appears in the result, and a redaction event is recorded; (5) search_symbols/references return the same cross-file resolution the Phase-1 index proved; (6) every primitive writes a metering entry to the ledger for the charged amount.
phase_task.docs: DESIGN.md: finalize the retrieval section — the primitive set, the token-accounting model (what a call costs and why span < file), and how budgeted retrieval + determinism enable replay. Add the metering "retrieval bytes/tokens" dimension to the metering section. Document the secret-redaction boundary as the first layer of the injection/secret-hygiene story (sandbox egress is the later backstop). Carry forward the two Phase-1 debts explicitly: (a) name+language-scoped resolution limitation restated in the retrieval section, (b) index-as-single-JSON scaling seam. Finalize ADR-0001 (retrieval model) — move from Proposed to Accepted, note the accounting model.
phase_task.stop: Do not start Phase 3 (sandbox). Report: the retrieval primitive signatures as implemented, the exact token-accounting formula (how cost is computed per primitive), the ledger reserve/commit interaction for a retrieval, the secret-redaction approach (what patterns, where applied, how logged), and how determinism is guaranteed across replay.
